mentions.title: WARNING about King Main Thrust Bearings
mentions.snippet: Explicit buyer-warning thread aimed at other builders about King main thrust bearings on diesel truck engines. Framed as a warning rather than a question, which makes it the most damaging single item on the list.
mentions.replyNote: Still returns HTTP 403 Forbidden; thread content could not be read.

mentions.title: No more King XP bearings
mentions.snippet: Builder reports a 2024 King main bearing confirmed out of spec by King's own tech line on the free-spread dimension, with a 2025 production run showing the same issue and no new production until January 2027. Points at a repeatable manufacturing problem, not a one-off part.
mentions.replyNote: King Bearings posted an official response dated 2026-08-04 explaining their eccentric bearing profile design and offering to investigate the specific parts if the builder supplies details.

mentions.title: King Main Bearings Defective
mentions.snippet: King STDX undersize sets reported with thrust bearings over 1mm too narrow to fit BMW S85 and S65 blocks, across multiple sets rather than a single part. Dimensional defect with a clear fitment consequence.
mentions.replyNote: Still 307-redirects to the tollbit.m5board.com mirror instead of returning thread content.

mentions.title: King Bearing - lack of professional help for quality control problem
mentions.snippet: Customer received an unopened package with a mismatched mix of undersize uppers and lowers and says King redirected them to their supplier rather than resolving it. Complaint is about service handling as much as the packing error.

mentions.title: King Bearing Failures?
mentions.snippet: King main and rod bearings reported damaged during break-in of a high-compression build, requiring crankshaft rework. Other posters question whether the bearing brand alone is responsible.
